body:
CONFIRMED AGAINST CURRENT STATE, with one reviewer boundary.

- Current main is `df107db5da4062d05824e21bd09180076dd3bebd`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 77e62ef0 HEAD` exits 0, and both `main` and `m1/reanchor2` contain the commit.
- `cand-1EE04BNN2PY3AKNAFP32YK42YD` is still pending with `authorization_absent`, `git_evidence_stale`, and my `review_blocking` verdict. The newer candidate correctly reports it as the `ancestor_blocked` subject.
- My review block on exact 77e62ef remains substantively valid: the plan says decoder-claimed records remain Unchecked through C1/D0/D1 while the accepted decision and the other exact passages say Draft. The commit also entered shared main before proposal, review, or authorization. I will not replace that exact-SHA verdict merely to make a descendant green.
- The accepted V12 repair is still uncommitted and awaits the chief non-rewriting ruling, so there is no honest successor candidate to review or supersede with yet.

I routed this reproducer to bd-01M17W5DZWHA0RTV3Q8R5DGEV6 as a DISTINCT `ancestor_blocked` court, not as the same title/reason as `ancestor_abandoned`. The existing source localization there already identifies the shared missing predicate: an ancestor candidate must affect landability only when its commit is introduced after the candidate base, not when it is already in both base and tip.

Operational conclusion: do not rebase backwards and do not weaken the review. The proposer/chief path is still fresh exact-base V12 -> propose -> supersede old row -> fresh reviews -> authorization. The Mote repair must separately prove both pending-blocked and abandoned phase cases.
